statements.text: The equation x + y = 15 is called the equation of first degree in two variables.
Solving this equation means finding an ordered pair of real numbers that satisfies the equation.
The equation can be solved by putting it in one of two forms: (1) y = 15 - x or (2) x = 15 - y. Formula: $y=15-x$ or $x=15-y$

If x ∈ R then the substitution set is R × R, so the equation of the first degree has infinitely many solutions, each an ordered pair (x, y) whose first projection is x and second projection is y. Formula: $R\times R$

context.text: By giving one of the two variables any value, you can calculate the value of the other variable.

Imagine you have exactly 12 pounds to spend at a school canteen, where a sandwich costs 3 pounds and a juice costs 2 pounds. If you buy $x$ sandwiches and $y$ juices, then $3x+2y=12$. Can you write this as $y=\ldots$, try different values of $x$ to find pairs $(x, y)$ that use all 12 pounds, and see what shape the points make when drawn?

Suppose Gym A charges 20 pounds to join plus 5 pounds per visit, so the cost of $x$ visits is $y=20+5x$. Suppose Gym B has no joining fee but charges 10 pounds per visit, so $y=10x$. If you draw both lines on the same graph, where do they meet, and what does that point tell you?

statements.text: Two simultaneous first-degree equations in two variables are solved by removing one of the two variables to get a first-degree equation in one variable. Solving it gives the value of that variable, and substituting in one of the given equations gives the value of the other variable, which was removed.

context.text: Imagine 2 notebooks and 1 pen cost 11 pounds, while 1 notebook and 1 pen cost 7 pounds. With $x$ as the price of a notebook and $y$ as the price of a pen, this gives $2x+y=11$ and $x+y=7$. Without drawing, how can you remove one variable to find the price of a notebook and of a pen?

Suppose a school play sold 30 tickets in total. Adult tickets cost 20 pounds and child tickets cost 10 pounds, and the total money collected was 450 pounds. If $x$ is the number of adult tickets and $y$ the number of child tickets, can you form two equations from this information and solve them to find how many of each kind were sold?
